content.title: About
content.content: Egg white is the clear liquid surrounding the yolk. It is rich in protein, virtually free of fat and carbohydrates, and contains small amounts of B‑vitamins and minerals such as selenium and potassium. Egg white is widely used to make omelets, scrambled eggs, or fried dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg white is about 90 % water and 10 % protein.
It contains all essential amino acids, making it a complete protein source.
When whipped, egg white forms a stable foam, ideal for meringues and soufflés.
Selenium in egg white supports antioxidant protection in the body.
Egg white is a staple in many diet plans because of its low calorie content.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: One large egg white provides roughly 3.6 g of protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Very low in fat
items.content: Egg white contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in selenium
items.content: Selenium helps maintain immune function and protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: A single egg white has about 17 kcal, useful for weight‑management regimes.

items.title: Heart‑friendly
items.content: Absence of cholesterol in egg white makes it safe for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg white, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Biotin binding
items.content: Raw egg whites contain avidin, which can bind biotin and lead to deficiency if consumed in excess.

items.title: Salmonella risk
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking can allow salmonella contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Egg whites can be prepared as an omelet, scrambled, or simply fried. For an omelet, whisk the whites with a pinch of salt, pour into a hot pan, and cook until set and lightly golden. Scrambled egg whites are cooked while continuously stirring until curds form. Fried egg whites are common in Asian cuisine, often seasoned with soy sauce and mixed with vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store egg whites in a sealed container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. Frozen egg whites keep for up to 6 months; thaw them in the fridge before use.
